title: Overlapping Intervals (Meeting Rooms)
prompt:
Given a list of intervals `intervals` where each interval is `[start, end]`, determine if a person could attend all meetings (i.e., no two intervals overlap).

**Approach:** Sort by start time, then check consecutive pairs for overlap.

**Requirements:**
1. Define and export `canAttendAll(intervals: number[][]): boolean` in `solution.ts`
2. Sort the intervals by start time using `.sort((a, b) => a[0] - b[0])`
3. Iterate through consecutive pairs of sorted intervals
4. If any interval starts before the previous one ends, return `false`
5. Return `true` if no overlaps found

**Notes:**
- Touching intervals `[1, 5]` and `[5, 10]` do NOT overlap (one ends when the other starts)
- An empty array means no meetings, so return `true`

**Examples:**
```typescript
canAttendAll([[0, 30], [5, 10], [15, 20]])  // false
canAttendAll([[7, 10], [2, 4]])             // true
canAttendAll([])                            // true
canAttendAll([[1, 5], [5, 10]])             // true
```

**Complexity:** O(n log n) time, O(n) space (for sorted copy)
hints: Sort the intervals by their start time first
Use [...intervals].sort((a, b) => a[0] - b[0]) to sort without mutating
Two intervals overlap if the second starts before the first ends
